subject: ss-pulmonology
title: Pulmonary hypertension: groups, echo probability and centre therapy

steps.tx: **Pulmonary hypertension** (**PH**) means mean pulmonary arterial pressure above **20 mmHg** on **right heart catheterisation**. Precapillary disease requires wedge pressure **15 mmHg** or less with vascular resistance above **2 Wood units**, so precise haemodynamics separate precapillary from postcapillary disease every time.
steps.say: PH is defined by pressures above twenty millimetres of mercury in practice. Right heart catheterisation confirms the diagnosis correctly in practice for patients. Wedge pressure and resistance separate the types reliably in PH centres.

steps.tx: Five groups organise the differential: **group 1** pulmonary arterial hypertension, **group 2** left heart disease, **group 3** lung disease or hypoxia, **group 4** chronic thromboembolic obstruction, and **group 5** unclear multifactorial disease. Groups **2** and **3** dominate in practice through valve disease and chronic lung disease burden.
steps.say: Five groups classify pulmonary hypertension for exams in detail for students learning. Left heart and lung disease cause most cases overall worldwide in series. Group one and group four have specific therapy available today.

rows: PAH idiopathic, heritable, connective tissue disease, HIV, portal hypertension

steps.tx: Symptoms progress from exertional breathlessness and fatigue to exertional chest pain, presyncope and syncope, with later ankle oedema, ascites, raised jugular venous pressure, loud **P2** and right ventricular heave. Rapid progression, **WHO functional class III to IV**, syncope, right heart failure signs or low output demand urgent **PH centre** referral.
steps.say: Breathlessness and fatigue start the story in most patients diagnosed with PH. Syncope and right heart failure indicate danger ahead in PH patients presenting daily. Functional class three or four requires urgent referral daily in practice for patients.

steps.tx: Echocardiography grades probability by peak **TR velocity** above **3.4 m/s** for high probability, **2.9 to 3.4 m/s** for intermediate, and **2.8 m/s** or less for low probability, adjusted by supporting signs. Other signs include right to left ventricular ratio above **1.0**, inferior vena cava above **21 mm**, pulmonary artery above **25 mm** and right atrial area above **18 cm2**.
steps.say: Echocardiography grades probability from TR velocity measurements daily in clinic. Above three point four means high probability in practice for clinicians. Supporting signs shift intermediate cases upward in grading performed daily.

steps.tx: First line tests include **ECG**, chest radiograph, **BNP** or NT proBNP, spirometry with volumes and **DLCO**, arterial blood gas and transthoracic echo. A **V/Q scan** screens for chronic thromboembolic disease and outperforms **CT angiography** for chronic clot, while cause hunting adds high resolution CT, autoimmune serology, **HIV** testing, liver assessment and thyroid and sleep studies.
steps.say: First line tests cover heart, lung and blood markers together in clinic. VQ scanning screens chronic clot better than CT imaging performed. Cause hunting includes serology and HIV testing in clinic practice.

steps.tx: **Right heart catheterisation** at a PH centre confirms type before any PAH specific drug, and **vasoreactivity testing** guides high dose calcium channel blocker therapy in idiopathic, heritable or drug associated PAH. General care uses **diuretics** for congestion, oxygen when arterial PO2 falls below **8 kPa**, iron correction, vaccination, supervised exercise, and pregnancy avoidance in PAH.
steps.say: Right heart catheterisation confirms PH before therapy starts always in practice. Vasoreactivity predicts blocker response in selected cases well for patients. Diuretics and oxygen support every group of PH patients daily.

left.title: Treat the cause first
points: Long term oxygen if PO2 below 8

steps.tx: Low or intermediate risk PAH without cardiopulmonary comorbidity starts with combination **endothelin receptor antagonist** plus **PDE5 inhibitor**, for example **ambrisentan** plus **tadalafil**. High risk disease adds an **IV or SC prostacyclin analogue** such as **treprostinil** and prompts transplant discussion, with reassessment every **3 to 6 months** using walk distance above **440 m** for low risk and NT proBNP below **300** for low risk.
steps.say: Low risk PAH starts with combination therapy for most patients treated. High risk disease needs prostacyclin early in care daily for patients presenting. Reassessment tracks walk distance and natriuretic peptides regularly in clinic.

steps.tx: **CTEPH** needs lifelong therapeutic anticoagulation, **pulmonary endarterectomy** for operable disease, and **balloon pulmonary angioplasty** or **riociguat** for inoperable or residual PH. In PH with interstitial disease, inhaled **treprostinil** may help, while **ambrisentan** stays not recommended in PH with idiopathic fibrosis and riociguat stays avoided in idiopathic interstitial pneumonia.
steps.say: CTEPH needs lifelong anticoagulation in every patient treated in clinic. Operable disease needs endarterectomy best of all treatments available in centres. Inoperable disease may need balloon angioplasty or riociguat daily in centres.

steps.tx: Traps include diagnosing PH from echo alone, since echo gives probability while catheterisation confirms disease, and starting **sildenafil** or other PAH drugs in group **2** or **3** without centre assessment. Excluding chronic clot on **CT angiography** alone fails because **V/Q scanning** is more sensitive, and combining PDE5 inhibitors with nitrates or riociguat risks severe hypotension.
steps.say: Echo only estimates probability in pulmonary hypertension always in practice. Catheterisation confirms PH before drug therapy starts in patients. CT scanning can miss chronic clot that VQ scanning finds in clinic.

steps.tx: High yield anchors: mean pressure above **20 mmHg** defines PH, wedge **15 mmHg** and resistance **2 Wood units** split types, TR velocity above **3.4 m/s** means high echo probability, walk above **440 m** marks low risk and below **165 m** marks high risk, NT proBNP below **300** low and above **1100** high, reassess every **3 to 6 months**. **Sildenafil** is **20 mg** three times daily, **tadalafil** **40 mg** daily and macitentan **10 mg** daily.
steps.say: Twenty millimetres is the defining cutoff for PH in practice daily for students learning. High echo probability needs TR above three point four in clinic. Walk and peptide thresholds guide escalation decisions in clinic practice.

rows: Wedge 15 or less, resistance above 2 Wood units
